subject: Re: Proposal — Ops credit swap in lieu of SLA penalty (billing cadence implications)

Subject: Private deploy commercial questions — ops credit idea

Hi Soojin / Vanessa,

Thanks for the proposal. A quick question from our side on the SLA penalty language: our procurement team would prefer to avoid open-ended cash offsets and instead apply any SLA-related remediation as a credit against future invoices or platform fees.

Specifically: would Redwood consider an "ops credit" approach (credit applied to platform fee amortization or future invoices) instead of monetary SLA refunds? Two follow-ups:
- How would that interact with billing cadence (we're on annual prepay today but considering quarterly invoicing for the first year)?
- Can you provide an example of how a penalty => credit swap would show up on an invoice (line items), and any cap you'd expect?

I've looped in procurement (procurement@clearsky.com). Happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Best,

Subject: Re: Private deploy commercial questions — ops credit idea

Hi Mike — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can structure SLA remediation as credits rather than cash refunds, and we have two common patterns customers choose from. Below are practical examples and constraints so procurement can evaluate.

Option A — Invoice credit (preferred for Clearsky):
- If an SLA breach is validated, Redwood issues a credit line item applied to the next invoice.
- Credit can be applied to the platform fee portion (amortized license) or to support retainer invoices; customer chooses which bucket at signing.
- Cap: typically we cap credits to a percent of the annual platform fee (common ranges 3–10%), and credits can’t reduce the invoice below any prepaid/committed minimums.

Option B — Ops retainer offset (engineering-action tied):
- Instead of a pure monetary offset, we apply a one-time ops-credit token to be consumed against professional services / SRE time (e.g., 40 hours of remediation) within X months.
- This is useful when customer wants guaranteed hands-on remediation rather than cash-equivalent credits.

Billing cadence considerations:
- Annual prepay: credits are typically tracked and applied as a lump sum against renewal or next invoice cycle.
- Quarterly/monthly: credits can be posted as a line item on the next invoice; smaller billing cadence gives faster visible realization of credits.

Example (from the SLA-credit-math.xlsx I attached):
- Annual platform fee: $600k/year (amortized monthly = $50k/mo)
- Validated SLA incident = 2% credit cap => $12k credit; posted as "SLA credit - August 2026" line item on next invoice.

Operational notes / constraints:
- We need clear definition of validation (postmortem + metric thresholds) and a 30-day review window to confirm credit.
- Legal needs to sign off on the contract language to ensure credits are non-prejudicial to other remedies.

Next steps: I can send a redline with both options and the sample invoice line template. Vanessa — can you confirm whether Clearsky prefers credits to apply against platform fee (license) vs support retainer? Mike / procurement — any preference on cap (we typically see 3–7% for strategic pilots, 5–10% for broader rollouts)?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

Mike / team — quick operational proposal from our side that often shortens procurement cycles:

Proposal summary (one-line): allow credits in-lieu-of-cash SLA refunds, posted as a distinct invoice line that offsets the platform fee, with a 6% annual cap and a time-bound consumption window of 12 months.

Details / rationale:
- Cap at 6% of annual platform fee for year one (protects Redwood from repeated large offsets while giving Clearsky meaningful recourse).
- Credits posted as "SLA credit" line item and auto-applied to the next invoice; if annual prepay, credits apply at renewal as a lump sum unless customer requests immediate pro-rated refund to operating budget.
- For critical incidents where Clearsky requests direct SRE intervention, we can instead convert credit to a professional-service engagement (ops retainer drawdown) so you get immediate engineering time.

Operational mechanics we need to agree on: breach validation cadence, credit posting SLA (30 days after validation), and whether credits reduce platform fee vs support retainer.

If you like this framing, we’ll ask legal to draft the amendment language and commercial to prepare a DocuSign-ready addendum with the invoice-line examples.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-credit-math.xlsx (example calc)

Subject: Re: Private deploy commercial questions — ops credit idea (legal draft notes)

Team / Jorge — quick legal notes before we issue the redline:
- We can accept credits in-lieu-of cash refunds with these guardrails:
  * Credits may be applied only against future Redwood invoices and do not constitute a cash refund.
  * Annual cap: 6% of the annual platform fee for the relevant 12-month period.
  * Credits shall be posted within 30 days after Redwood and Customer sign-off on the incident validation (postmortem).
  * Credits are non-transferable and expire 12 months after issuance.
- Conversion clause: Customer may elect one-time conversion of available credit to a professional-services SRE engagement; conversion reduces the available credit dollar-for-dollar and Redwood will provide an SOW for the engagement.
- Important: include language excluding credits from affecting any committed minimums or reducing fees that trigger reserved-capacity computations.

I drafted the amendment language and attached the redline (draft_amendment_redlined.docx). Once Soojin confirms the commercial terms (cap, bucket), I’ll finalize and circulate to Jorge for procurement redline.

-David Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft_amendment_redlined.docx (legal redline - contains proposed clause and invoice sample text)
